title: Moving Stones Until Consecutive
summary: Given three stones at distinct positions on the X-axis, represented by integers a, b, and c, determine the minimum and maximum number of moves required to align the stones consecutively.
statement: Given three stones at distinct positions on the X-axis, represented by integers a, b, and c, determine the minimum and maximum number of moves required to align the stones consecutively. A move involves picking an endpoint stone and placing it in an unoccupied position between the other two stones, ensuring the new position is not the middle stone's current position.
constraints: Return minimum and maximum legal moves to consecutive positions.
hints: Sort positions and inspect the two empty gaps.
A gap of zero or one permits a one-move finish; otherwise two endpoint moves are required.
Maximum moves consume every empty position across both gaps.
Endpoint moves can close one gap per move, while the shortcut precisely captures placing an endpoint beside the other two.
editorial: Endpoint moves can close one gap per move, while the shortcut precisely captures placing an endpoint beside the other two.

tests.explanation: Move five to three for the minimum one; the maximum is two.
The stones are already consecutive, so both counts are zero.
